lesson_title: The Dam That Gives Itself Away
hook_text: A dark patch on your orthophoto. Is it a dam, a car park or a ploughed field? One contour line settles it.
clip_script: Straight-down photos hide hills. Everything looks flat. So the orthophoto cheats: it prints contour lines over the picture, every 5 metres of height. Now look at that dark, smooth patch. Dam? Car park? Ploughed field? Here is the test. Water in a bath is always flat. So the edge of a dam is all at one height, and a line joining points at one height is a contour. If the edge of the dark patch runs right along a contour, it is water. And look where it sits: at the narrow end of a valley, where the contour V's squeeze together. Short wall, big lake. Now that pale line crossing the hill, with contours bunching in on both sides? A road in a cutting, sliced through the hill. And those sharp V's on a bare slope with no river? Dongas, gullies torn out by rain. Photo plus contours. Two clues. One answer.
visual_style: An orthophoto with a dark patch; a bath of water levels flat and morphs into the dam; a contour line glows exactly along the shoreline; the valley V's squeeze at a straight wall; a road cutting appears with bunching contours; pale dongas branch on a slope.
pacing: Mystery hook, slow bath reveal, quick cutting and dongas, punchy close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to read heights in 5 metre steps, calculate gradient at 1:10 000 and link the orthophoto to the topographic map.
